newsitem.title: IRAN: NIOC manager details offshore oil development.
newsitem.headline: NIOC manager details offshore oil development.

text.p: National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC) plans to double its offshore crude output by the turn of the decade through a combination of foreign investment and field development work by NIOC and other Iranian firms.
The following are excerpts from an interview with NIOC Offshore director Seyed Jalilian on Saturday.
-Offshore output target. Current level of production is 550,000 barrels per day (bpd) and our long term production goal is over one million bpd by the turn of the century.

-Work by NIOC and other Iranian firms. Our expansion activity at Abuzar, Doroud, Foroozan, Bahregansar, Nowruz and Sirri C and D fields over the next several years will provide an additional 300,000 bpd or so.
Development drilling is expected to start at Abuzar at the end of February as part of plans to lift its current output of 130,000 bpd to 200,000 bpd at the turn of the decade.
-Fields with existing or potential foreign role.

Sirri E and A. In Sirri A, production will start by the end of 1997 and in Sirri E by the end of 1998...Project progress is according to the program, more than ten percent...Delineation drilling is completed and fabrication of well platforms will soon begin (in Bandar Abbas).
Jalilian said seismic work had led to an upwards revision in the size of recoverable reserves at the fields but that studies were needed to finalise the size of reserves.
Soroush, Balal. Final proposals of the interested companies have been received by NIOC and the winners will be announced by the end of March 1997.
Doroud. There have been some changes in scope of work because of the priority of water injection system and the subject is under consideration.

South Pars. John Brown Engineering has completed offshore engineering and design work on the first phase development. First phase envisages the construction of two offshore platform jackets... Work on the platforms is currently under way at a fabrication yard operated by (local engineering firm) Sadra in Bandar Abbas.

On the second and third phases, offers of different companies are received and the subject is under discussion. Many companies they are looking at this project. It is not only (French oil firm) Total SA.

Henjam. With the great intention of Oman in participating in development project of Henjam, disussions are underway. The percentage of each country has been settled 80 percent Iran and 20 percent Oman.
Jalilian said that NIOC Offshore was also looking to develop further offshore fields with foreign partners. These included fields in the Strait of Hormuz. -U.S. sanctions impact.

The important problem we faced, was securing essential spare parts and maintenance from some American manufacturer which has temporarily inhibited production at one offshore field by an estimated 25,000 bpd. Sanctions do not stop NIOC Offshore's aggressive well work-over, development and drilling plans. NIOC Offshore for new projects will not use U.S. equipment.
